content: 1. High-dose or multiple-dose NSAIDs can increase the risk of nephrotoxicity when co-administered with tenofovir DF. Alternatives to NSAIDs should be considered to mitigate this risk. 2. Co-administration of tenofovir DF and trospium chloride can lead to increased levels of both drugs due to reduced renal clearance. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 3. Tucatinib increases the levels or effects of tenofovir DF by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Consider reducing the dosage of P-gp substrates, especially when small concentration changes could result in severe or life-threatening toxicities. 4. Ublituximab reduces the effects of tenofovir DF through immunosuppressive mechanisms, increasing the risk of infection. Therapy should be modified, and patients monitored closely. 5. Vadadustat increases the levels or effects of tenofovir DF through mechanisms involving other pathways. It may also increase the exposure of BCRP substrates. Monitor for adverse effects of BCRP substrates and adjust their doses according to product labeling. 6. Valacyclovir increases the levels of tenofovir DF through mechanisms involving renal function or active tubular secretion. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration with drugs that reduce renal function or compete for active tubular secretion may elevate serum concentrations of tenofovir. 7. Valganciclovir increases the levels of tenofovir DF through similar mechanisms. Use caution and monitor closely, as co-administration with drugs affecting renal function or tubular secretion can elevate tenofovir levels. 8. Co-administration of tenofovir DF and vancomycin increases the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Tenofovir DF increases the levels of verapamil by reducing renal clearance, potentially leading to increased toxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Co-administration of tenofovir DF and voclosporin increases the toxicity of both drugs due to nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Therapy should be modified, and patients monitored closely. Drugs associated with nephrotoxicity may heighten the risk of acute or chronic nephrotoxicity. 11. Tenofovir DF and zidovudine both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Co-administration of black cohosh and tenofovir DF may increase the toxicity of either drug due to pharmacodynamic synergism, with a potential risk of hepatotoxicity. The clinical significance is unknown, but close monitoring is advised. 13. Paromomycin and tenofovir DF both increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Paromomycin also increases tenofovir DF levels by reducing elimination. The clinical significance is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 14. Abacavir and tenofovir DF both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Acalabrutinib increases the levels of tenofovir DF by inhibiting intestinal BCRP. Monitor closely for adverse reactions and consider dose adjustments for BCRP substrates. 16. Acyclovir and tenofovir DF both increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Acyclovir also increases tenofovir DF levels through mechanisms involving renal function or tubular secretion. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Adefovir and tenofovir DF increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism, leading to enhanced nephrotoxicity. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 18. Aldesleukin increases the levels of tenofovir DF by reducing renal clearance, and both drugs increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Amikacin and tenofovir DF both increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Amikacin also increases tenofovir DF levels by reducing elimination. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Tenofovir DF increases the levels of amiloride by reducing renal clearance, potentially leading to increased toxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Amphotericin B (cholesteryl sulfate, deoxycholate, liposomal, or phospholipid complex formulations) and tenofovir DF both increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Co-administration may also increase tenofovir levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Apalutamide decreases the levels or effects of tenofovir DF by increasing elimination. It weakly induces BCRP, potentially reducing systemic exposure to BCRP substrates. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Tenofovir DF decreases the levels of atazanavir through an unknown mechanism. Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Co-administration of tenofovir DF with atidarsagene autotemcel is contraindicated. Antiretroviral medications may interfere with the manufacturing of atidarsagene autotemcel. Avoid ARTs for at least one month before cell mobilization and during the expected duration of medication elimination. 25. Bacitracin and tenofovir DF both increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Avoid concurrent use of bacitracin with other nephrotoxic drugs. 26. Berotralstat increases the levels or effects of tenofovir DF by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Monitor or titrate the P-gp substrate dose if co-administered. 27. Betibeglogene autotemcel and tenofovir DF should not be co-administered. Antiretroviral medications may interfere with the manufacturing of apheresis cells. Avoid ARTs for at least one month before mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed. 28. Bleomycin increases the levels of tenofovir DF by reducing renal clearance, potentially leading to increased toxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Capreomycin and tenofovir DF both increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Carboplatin and tenofovir DF both increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Co-administration may also increase tenofovir levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Celecoxib and tenofovir DF increase each other's levels by reducing renal clearance. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 32. Cidofovir and tenofovir DF both increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Cidofovir also increases tenofovir DF levels through mechanisms involving renal function or tubular secretion. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Cimetidine and tenofovir DF increase each other's levels by reducing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Cisplatin and tenofovir DF both increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Cisplatin also increases tenofovir DF levels by reducing elimination. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Colistin and tenofovir DF both increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Iodinated contrast media and tenofovir DF both increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 37. Cyclosporine and tenofovir DF both increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 38. Tenofovir DF decreases the levels or effects of dabigatran by inducing the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid co-administration. 39. Danicopan increases the levels or effects of tenofovir DF by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Monitor closely and consider dose reduction of P-gp substrates. 40. Darolutamide increases the levels or effects of tenofovir DF by inhibiting BCRP. Avoid co-administration with BCRP inhibitors. If unavoidable, monitor closely for adverse reactions and consider dose reduction of BCRP substrate drugs. 41. Dichlorphenamide and tenofovir DF both decrease serum potassium levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Diclofenac and tenofovir DF increase each other's levels by reducing renal clearance. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 43. Didanosine toxicity is increased by tenofovir DF due to reduced elimination. This may elevate the risk of pancreatitis. Reduce the didanosine dose to 250 mg/day if weight >60 kg and to 200 mg/day if weight <60 kg. Monitor closely. 44. Diflunisal and tenofovir DF increase each other's levels by reducing renal clearance. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 45. Tenofovir DF increases the levels of digoxin by reducing renal clearance, potentially leading to increased toxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Tenofovir DF increases the levels of dofetilide by reducing renal clearance, potentially leading to increased toxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Tenofovir DF decreases the levels or effects of duvelisib by inducing the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 48. Tenofovir DF decreases the levels or effects of edoxaban by inducing the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid co-administration with potent P-gp inducers. 49. Efavirenz and tenofovir DF both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 50. Elagolix increases the levels or effects of tenofovir DF by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 51. Elivaldogene autotemcel and tenofovir DF should not be co-administered. Antiretroviral medications may interfere with stem cell mobilization. Avoid ARTs for at least one month before initiating stem cell mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed. 52. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF is a complete regimen for HIV and should not be co-administered with other antiretrovirals. This combination is contraindicated. 53. Emtricitabine and tenofovir DF both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 54. Enasidenib increases the levels or effects of tenofovir DF by inhibiting OATP1B1, OATP1B3, or BCRP substrates. Avoid co-administration. If unavoidable, reduce the substrate dosage and monitor closely. 55. Encorafenib increases the levels or effects of tenofovir DF by inhibiting BCRP. Monitor closely for signs of increased exposure and consider dose adjustments. 56. Enfuvirtide and tenofovir DF both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 57. Tenofovir DF increases the levels of entecavir by reducing renal clearance, potentially leading to increased toxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 58. Etodolac and tenofovir DF increase each other's levels by reducing renal clearance. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 59. Tenofovir DF increases the levels of famciclovir by reducing renal clearance, potentially leading to increased toxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 60. Fenofibrate increases the levels of tenofovir DF by reducing renal clearance, increasing the risk of myopathy. Use caution and monitor closely. 61. Fenofibrate micronized and fenofibric acid similarly increase the levels of tenofovir DF, with an associated risk of myopathy. Use caution and monitor closely. 62. Fenoprofen and tenofovir DF increase each other's levels by reducing renal clearance. Modify therapy and monitor closely.
